BEFORE YOU GO

Winter sports essentials

Everything you need for a Yatsugatake ski trip — gear, transport, snow conditions, and après-ski.

🎿

Ski Gear & Rentals

  • All three ski areas have rental shops — skis, boots, poles and helmets available on-site. Reserve online for the best availability in peak season.
  • Bring a good base layer and a waterproof shell. Yatsugatake snow is typically cold and dry, so heavy insulation is less critical than wind protection.
  • Helmets are strongly recommended and increasingly common — some resorts require them for children.
  • Ski lockers and boot drying rooms are standard at all resorts and most ski-focused accommodations.
🚄

Getting There

  • Azusa limited express from Shinjuku to Kobuchizawa takes ~2 hours (¥3,680 one way). Reserve seats in advance for peak ski weekends.
  • A rental car from Kobuchizawa Station gives flexibility to hit multiple resorts in one trip — highly recommended.
  • Risonare and Bleston Court run free ski shuttles to nearby resorts — factor this in when choosing accommodation.
  • IC cards (Suica / PASMO) work on the JR Chuo Line and most local buses. Top up at any major station.
❄️

Snow & Conditions

  • Peak powder season is mid-January to mid-February. December and March offer uncrowded slopes with good snow at elevation.
  • Yatsugatake's high base elevations (1,000–1,500 m) mean reliable snow even in lower-snowfall years.
  • Check resort websites for daily snow reports. Most publish grooming maps and webcam feeds.
  • New Year's and early February are peak crowd periods — weekday skiing is significantly more enjoyable.
♨️

Onsen & Après-ski

  • Most accommodations have onsen (hot spring baths) — essential recovery after a day on snow. Many are outdoor (rotenburo) and stay open even in snow.
  • Kobuchizawa's wine-road area has several good dinner spots — book Café Rosa in advance for weekend evenings.
  • Convenience stores are excellent for on-mountain snacks and pre-ski breakfasts — 7-Eleven rice balls and hot drinks are a staple.
  • Carry cash for small mountain restaurants and lift ticket supplements — card acceptance is limited at some facilities.
